hypotheses.justification: The theorem takes this instance because it is instance-implicit and `ℓ` is one of its arguments (through `conjL M H ℓ`). Nothing in the statement or the proof needs it. In `Definitions/Def_CohCarrier_Level.lean`, `GammaHUpper` (an abbrev for `(Gamma0Upper ℓ).subgroupOf (GammaH M H)`), `dvd_of_mem_GammaHUpper`, `conjUpperMat` and `conjL` all sit in section `Operators`, whose only variables are `(M : ℕ) (H : Subgroup (ZMod M)ˣ) (ℓ : ℕ)`. They take no `NeZero ℓ`. Only `heckeT` and the `FiniteIndex` instance ask for `[NeZero ℓ]` explicitly. `resK`, `jEquiv`, `jEquiv_mem_upper_iff` and `charInvolution` do not take it either. The proof is `MonoidHom.ext`, then `simp` with `comp_apply`, `toMultiplicativeRight_apply_apply`, `charInvolution_apply` and `toMul_ofMul`, then `congr 2`, then a rewrite with `jEquiv_apply` and `jEquiv_conjL`. `jEquiv_conjL` is stated in section `JConj`, whose variables are `(M H ℓ)` with no `NeZero`. So none of these steps uses the instance. Adding `omit [NeZero ℓ] in` lets the same statement and proof go through for every `ℓ`, including `ℓ = 0`.
